Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the opposite party no. 1- State and Mr. Sharad Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2.
2.

Application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed challenging summoning order dated 19.05.2017 as well as entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 26 of 2017 (Asharam versus Shyamoo and others) in which process has been issued under Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Soraon, District-Allahabad pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 4, Allahabad Shyamoo Prajapati And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicants submits that an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was filed on 05.10.2016 under Sections 419, 420, 499, 503, 509 and 120-B I.P.C. indicating the date and time of occurrence as 22.09.2016 at 2.00 pm.

4. It is submitted that the allegations of demand of dowry have been made against the applicants whereafter statement under Section 200 Cr.P.C. was recorded and by means of order dated 19.05.2017, process has been issued to the applicants under Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
5. Learned counsel for applicants has drawn attention to another F.I.R. registered as Case Crime No.
0530 dated 31.10.2016 to submit that the alleged victim being the daughter of opposite party no. 2 was in fact having an affair with another person with whom she had eloped resulting in filing of the aforesaid F.I.R.
It is submitted that the informant in the said F.I.R. is the complainant in the present case.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the marriage discussions were broken off once the applicants came to know about the affair of the victim with another person and there was no occasion for the trial court to have issued process under Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has also drawn attention to the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in the F.I.R. lodged as Case Crime No. 530 of 2016 indicating that victim had admitted her elopement with another person.

7. Learned counsel for opposite parties have refuted the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the applicants with the submission that the aspect of the first information report registered as Case Crime No. 530 of 2016 is completely different from the present complaint in which allegations have clearly being made and substantiated with regard to Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act under which cognizance have been taken.
8.

Upon consideration of submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perusal of material on record, it is quite evident that present proceedings arise out of the application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. in which allegation of dowry demand has been levelled against the applicants.
The cognizance order while issuing process has adverted to the aforesaid complaint, the case dairy and statements under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.

The aspect of elopement of the victim in the F.I.R. registered as Case Crime No. 530 of 2016, may not have applicability in the present facts and circumstances where prima facie satisfaction has been recorded by trial court while issuing process pertaining to Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The said factor of course may be taken as defence by the applicants which will be required to be considered by trial court at the appropriate stage.
At present, there does not appear any occasion to interfere with the order impugned.
9. In view of the facts and circumstances, the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. fails and is dismissed.
10. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicants submits that liberty may be granted to the applicants to file the discharge application.
